page: Vultr vx1-m-96c-768gb is a memory-optimized virtual server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance configuration does not include local SSD or NVMe storage, instead providing a minimal 1 GB of network-attached storage. It lacks integrated GPU hardware accelerators, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or deep learning workloads. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The high density of dedicated AMD cores combined with a substantial memory footprint offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets without the overhead of local storage maintenance. This profile is designed for memory-intensive applications, large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
